title: Dispatch: bootstrap ledger and 2n1t reconciliation corrections (attempt 2)
description:
SUPERVISOR REVIEW OF ATTEMPT 1 (eshyra-o9bd.19.5.1.1, commit 5c5ca93).
Attempt 1's reconciliation REASONING is good — per-bead argument, explicit
refusal to auto-reopen, and a well-argued "why no PREMATURE CLOSURE" section.
Keep all of it. Two defects make the deliverable incomplete.

=== FILES YOU OWN ===
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.json
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/bootstrap-capability-ledger.md
  docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/2n1t-engine-closure-reconciliation.md
  packages/core/src/rules/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.ts
  packages/core/test/bootstrapCapabilityLedger.test.ts

=== DEFECT 1: THE RECONCILIATION OMITS NINE OF TWELVE CHILDREN ===
This is the important one. The document reconciles only eshyra-2n1t,
eshyra-2n1t.1 and eshyra-2n1t.2 — and .1/.2 are the two PRODUCT-DECISION
children (multiclass scope, creation-variant policy). The children that actually
claimed engine capability completeness were skipped entirely:

  eshyra-2n1t.3   F1: Dice-grammar extension (advantage/disadvantage, keep/drop)
  eshyra-2n1t.4   F2: Action-economy turn budget
  eshyra-2n1t.5   F3: Concentration & active-effect lifecycle
  eshyra-2n1t.7   F5: Usage/recharge, resource & attunement state
  eshyra-2n1t.8   F6: Death, dying & HP-buffer state
  eshyra-2n1t.9   F7: Rest engine (short/long rest)
  eshyra-2n1t.11  F9: Deterministic resolution & derived-math primitives
  eshyra-2n1t.12  F10: Canonical currency & trade gameplay surface
  eshyra-2n1t.13  Enforce fail-closed single-class character boundary

Run `bd show eshyra-2n1t` and read its CHILDREN list to get the complete set —
do not trust the list above to be exhaustive; there may be a .6 and a .10.
Reconcile EVERY child, plus eshyra-b69j.13, eshyra-o9bd.18.7 and
eshyra-o9bd.18.7.8 (attempt 1 already covered those last three; keep them).

These nine are the entire reason the deliverable exists: the audit found 794
engine-pending magic-item clauses three days after they closed claiming engine
capability work was done. Classifying only the two design-decision children
leaves that contradiction unexamined.

For each child: read its description, acceptance criteria and close reason, then
argue the classification PER BEAD — DIFFERENT SCOPE OR TAXONOMY | STALE READINESS
MAPPING | INCOMPLETE INTEGRATION | PREMATURE CLOSURE. Do not classify by number
similarity: eshyra-2n1t's F1-F10 is a DIFFERENT taxonomy from the pack's
engine:F1-F10 (that epic's F1 was dice grammar, F4 spell-slot economy, F8
character-build gaps, F9 derived math, F10 currency). Only F2/F3/F5/F7 roughly
correspond, and even those must be checked rather than assumed.

Attempt 1 concluded no bead warrants PREMATURE CLOSURE. That conclusion was
reached without examining these nine, so re-derive it rather than restating it.
It may well survive — but INCOMPLETE INTEGRATION is the likely answer for
several, given that primitives such as usage/recharge state exist in code yet
794 magic-item clauses remain engine-pending.

Still: preserve historical truth. Do not reopen, close, or modify any bead.
Record reopen/corrective recommendations as data in the document; the supervisor
executes them.

=== DEFECT 2: THE LEDGER IS A FAMILY-LABEL RESTATEMENT, NOT AN INVENTORY ===
The ledger has exactly ten rows — one per engine:F* family. The spec asked for
`requirement` to name "the specific primitive, not the family label", and for
the ledger to be the instrument that lets every missing hook find an owner. One
row per family cannot do that: engine:F5 alone carries 399 hook references
spanning charges, recharge scheduling, attunement, curse persistence and
per-instance state, which are distinct primitives with distinct implementations.

It also makes two acceptance criteria vacuous: "every engine:F1..F10 appears at
least once" is trivially true, and "every row maps to an existing bead" is
trivially true because the ten family epics exist.

Rebuild the ledger at PRIMITIVE granularity. Expect several rows per family.
Derive them from:
  * `record.data.executionReadiness` in the committed pack — group the hooks by
    what they actually require, not by family label;
  * the 2026-07-06 inventories already in docs/audits/dnd5e-srd-5.1-final/
    (engine-coverage-inventory, execution-boundary-classification,
    rule-classification, magic-item-mechanics-inventory and siblings);
  * @eshyra/core as it exists today, for codeEvidence;
  * the audit findings in /mnt/d/eshyra-2026-07-24-audit-repair-bead-plan.md;
  * source clauses known to be missing from projection.

Consequences to handle:
  * `ownershipStatus` must now genuinely vary. Attempt 1 has all ten rows
    "owned". Some primitives will fit no existing bead — mark those
    `proposed-new-bead` with a proposed title and parent, as DATA. Do not
    create beads.
  * The non-pack-discovery proof must not rest on a single row. Assert that
    SEVERAL rows are discoverable only from non-pack sources, and keep the
    legendary-action budget as the worked example.
  * Keep the ledger labelled NON-AUTHORITATIVE in both JSON and .md.

=== UNCHANGED CONSTRAINTS FROM ATTEMPT 1 ===
No hand-copied counts (83, 226, 31, 169, 391, 399, 46, 15, 310, 236, 9, 794,
1016, 1813) — commit queries, not numbers. Qualified engine:F* IDs only. Records
use the `key` field, not `id`; executionReadiness lives at
`record.data.executionReadiness`. The bd-reference check must skip gracefully
when the `bd` binary is absent.

=== ENVIRONMENT AND VERIFICATION ===
This worktree already contains attempt 1's committed work; you are extending it,
not starting over. Run `npm ci` FIRST (worktrees have no node_modules of their
own). Run `npm run verify:worktree` BEFORE committing — it rewrites files.

=== HARD CONSTRAINTS ===
* Edit ONLY the files listed under FILES YOU OWN. A sibling dispatch is running
  in parallel on a disjoint file set. Do not touch package.json,
  packages/core/package.json, or packages/core/src/internal.ts.
* Do NOT modify any bead except your own. Do NOT run `bd dolt push`.
* Do NOT push, do NOT open or comment on a PR, do NOT merge. Committed work on
  your branch is a complete handoff.
* Do NOT weaken, skip, or delete any existing test. Do NOT regenerate the pack.
* Do not "fix" attempt 1 by deleting its work; the defects below are gaps in
  coverage and fidelity, not wrong direction.
